:::

Will came to lung disease by way of structural pharmacology. He trained in the
Medical Scientist Training Program at Vanderbilt University, where his doctoral
work with Heidi Hamm addressed the mechanism by which receptors activate
heterotrimeric G proteins. He moved to Boston for residency in internal medicine
at Massachusetts General Hospital and for fellowship in the Harvard Combined
Pulmonary and Critical Care program, where his clinical research used invasive
cardiopulmonary exercise testing to characterize unexplained exertional dyspnea.
He began working on cell metabolism during a research fellowship with Joseph
Loscalzo at Brigham and Women's Hospital, and started his own laboratory in 2015.
He is an attending physician in pulmonary and critical care medicine.
